Expectation1: Look out for each other's safety and well-being
Situation1: One sibling is about to cross the street without looking for oncoming traffic.
Expectation2: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation2: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Story: It was just past midnight when my phone buzzed, jolting me awake. My friend’s name flashed on the screen, and as soon as I answered, I heard her sobbing. She could barely get the words out—her family had just gotten terrible news, and she needed someone to talk to. I sat up, trying to focus, listening to her pain, wanting to be the friend she needed, to offer comfort and support. But then, through the thin wall, I heard the creak of the front door. My stepbrother, restless as always, was heading outside. I peeked out the window and saw him, barefoot, shuffling toward the street, not even glancing at the traffic. My heart pounded. I was torn—my friend’s voice trembled in my ear, desperate for me to stay, to listen, to care. But my stepbrother was steps away from danger, and I was supposed to look out for him, to keep him safe. I stood frozen, phone pressed to my ear, caught between two worlds, each demanding all of me at once.
